# Tobit Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Tobias answered his father: "I will do everything you have commanded me, Father.

**2** But how can I receive the money from him, when he does not know me and I do not know him? What token shall I give him so that he will recognize me, trust me, and hand over the money? And I don't know the roads of Media that lead there."

**3** Tobit answered his son Tobias: "He gave me a promissory note and I gave him one; I split it in two and we each took one half. I placed my half with the money. And now, it has been twenty years since I deposited that money. So now, my son, find yourself a trustworthy man to travel with you, and we will pay him wages when we return; and go and retrieve the money from Gabael."

**4** Tobias went out to find such a man, and he found Raphael the angel standing there — but he did not know that he was an angel.

**5** He said to him, "Are you able to come with me to Rages in Media? Do you know the region there?"

**6** The angel said to him, "I can go with you; I know the region, and I have stayed as a guest with our kinsman Gabael."

**7** Tobias said to him, "Wait here for me, and I will tell my father."

**8** He went in and told his father: "Look, Father — I have found a man from our own brothers, one of the sons of Israel."

Tobit said, "Call him in to me, so that I may find out what tribe he is from and whether he is a trustworthy companion for the journey."

**9** Tobias went out and called him: "Young man, my father is asking for you."

He came in, and Tobit greeted him first. Raphael said, "May you have every joy."

Tobit replied, "What joy is left to me? I am a blind man who cannot see the light of heaven. I dwell in darkness like the dead who see the light no more. I am among the living dead — I hear voices but see nothing."

Raphael said to him, "Take heart; God's healing for you is close at hand. Take heart."

Tobit said to him, "My son Tobias wishes to go to Media. Can you guide him and lead him on the way? I will pay you wages, brother."

He said, "I am able to go with him. I know the roads, and I have stayed with our kinsman Gabael, who lives at Rages in Media. It is two days' journey from Ecbatana to Rages, for Rages lies in the hill country."

**10** Tobit said to him, "Tell me, brother, what tribe and family are you from?"

**11** He said, "What tribe are you looking for? And what family?"

Tobit said, "I want to know, brother, what your tribe is and what your name is."

**12** He said, "I am Azariah, the son of the great Ananias, one of your own kinsmen."

**13** Tobit said, "Welcome and safe arrival, brother! Do not be angry with me for wanting to know your tribe and family — it turns out you are my brother indeed, from a good and excellent family. I knew Ananias and Nathan, the sons of the great Shemaiah, when we journeyed to Jerusalem together to worship, and we offered the firstborn offerings and the tithes of the produce. They were not led astray in the error of our brethren. You are from a great family, brother.

**14** But tell me: what wages shall I give you? A drachma a day, and what you need just as I provide for my own son?

**15** And if you bring him back safely, I will add a bonus to your wages."

And so they came to an agreement.

**16** Tobit said to Tobias: "My son, prepare yourself for the journey and set out with your brother. May God in heaven prosper your journey, and may his angel accompany you."

They both set out to go, and the young man's dog followed along with them, going behind them.

**17** His mother Hannah wept and said to Tobit: "Why have you sent my child away? Is he not the staff of our hands — does he not go in and out before us?

**18** Do not heap money upon money; let it be as a ransom for our child.

**19** For the life the Lord has granted us is enough for us."

**20** Tobit said to her, "Do not be troubled, my sister. He will go out in safety and return to us safely, and your own eyes will see him.

**21** For a good angel will accompany him, his journey will be blessed, and he will return safe."

Then she stopped weeping.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **v. 3**: "Promissory note" for Greek *cheirographon* (χειρόγραφον) — literally "hand-written document." The note split in half functions as a matching token, an ancient authentication method. "Note of hand" (EMET) is archaic; "promissory note" is formal and precise.
- **v. 4**: "standing there" added for natural English; the Greek *euron* (found) implies encounter. The narrator's statement "he did not know that he was an angel" is left exactly where it falls — the dramatic irony belongs to the reader, not to Tobias.
- **v. 9**: "Living dead" — Greek *nekros zōn* (living-corpse). LOGOS renders this as "I am among the living dead" rather than the literal oxymoron, preserving the emotional weight while maintaining intelligibility.
- **v. 12**: "Azariah" (Ἀζαρίας) — preserved as proper name throughout. Its meaning ("the LORD has helped") forms ironic commentary on the narrative.
- **v. 13**: "Nathan" — Sinaiticus reads *Iathān*; LOGOS uses "Nathan" as the standard English form of the name. Shemaiah is the patriarch of the priestly family claimed.
- **v. 16**: The dog — retained as a narrative detail unique to the longer Sinaiticus recension (GII). It serves as a marker of the journey and reappears in ch. 11.
- **v. 17**: "Staff of our hands" — Hebrew idiom for "our support / our help." Retained in formal equivalence rather than paraphrased. — LOGOS
